service_boundary: Represents the Chutes hosting service, not the underlying decentralised network protocol or the open-weight models it serves.
regional_controls: Capacity comes from a decentralised operator network rather than named regions, and no customer control over processing geography is documented.
retention_controls: The terms state that API requests, responses, and application content are not used to train models, and that content is not logged for public inference. Customer-created deployments are noted as running code the operator does not control.
routing: Requests reach a named open-weight model on network capacity; private deployments run on dedicated hardware billed by time.
customization: Customers can deploy their own model code and weights as private endpoints on dedicated hardware.
strengths: Confidential-compute execution is marked on every model in the public catalogue rather than offered as a premium tier.
Capacity comes from a decentralised operator network rather than a single cloud, which changes the concentration risk profile.
The platform's own core is published under a permissive licence, which is uncommon among hosted inference operators.
tradeoffs: The catalogue is open-weight only, so it is not an alternative for reaching proprietary frontier models.
The operating entity is unclear, with no named legal company and a team page listing mostly handles.
A pricing path on the operator's own site returns a not-found body under a success status, which would mislead automated checks.
